**Ileusoperationer uden iskæmi eller perforation** (ileus operations without ischemia or perforation) is a specific medical procedure category used in Danish acute surgery quality assessments. It serves as the defining patient cohort (the denominator) for [[indikator-4y|Indikator 4y]], a clinical quality indicator that measures the speed of surgical treatment for this specific group [^src1]. 

This procedure category is clinically differentiated from more severe acute abdominal conditions. While patients suffering from ischemia or bowel perforation fall under a more acute group requiring surgery within a strict 6-hour window (tracked by Indikator 4x), patients undergoing ileus operations without ischemia or perforation are required to be treated within a 24-hour timeframe [^src1]. Specifically, the indicator measures the proportion of these patients who are operated on within 24 hours of arriving at the hospital, out of all such patients who are operated on within a maximum of 48 hours [^src1].

In the context of the annual indicator report from the Acute Surgery Database (Akut Kirurgi Databasen), this metric is part of a broader national framework aimed at reducing wait times and improving survival rates for acute abdominal conditions. The most recent annual assessment revealed that 81.7% of patients in this category were operated on within the 24-hour target [^src2]. While this figure sits close to the national development target of ≥90%, it represents a marginal decrease from the previous year, highlighting a continued need for improvement in treatment speed for non-ischemic ileus patients across the healthcare system [^src2].
